title: The Dixie Cats and the musicians on Jones's first gig
summary: Jones names the likely first-gig band, including Eddie Winston, Sonny Gammond and the Alexis brothers, one of whom played string bass.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I don't remember. It's been a long time since I've been out there. Well, anyway, damn I hate getting in the middle of stories, but how do you spell Dixie Cats? Your band?
That was D-I-X-I-E-C-A-T-S. Oh no, it was one word. One word? D-I-X-I-E-C-A-T-S.
Yeah. And do you remember the band on your first gig that you went on? Those guys, who they would have been?

Yeah, I can give you a pretty good idea. Probably Eddie Winston on clarinet. We had a guy by the name of Murphy, but I can't remember if that was his first name or his second name. He was a trombone player. Probably Larry Mohobarack on piano. And maybe Charlie Mays on guitar. And Sonny Gammond, Vaughn Gammond Jr. was the drummer. That's probably generally who it was. I don't remember if we had a bass player in those days. Bass fiddle was an awfully hard instrument to find. It wasn't that many people played. Bobby Alexis played with us. But Bobby was, for some reason or another, Bobby wasn't always available. I don't know if he was in, if his school hours were different or what, but he was just about my age. But he later on went up to LSU. His brother was, all three brothers were very good musicians. One of them went to school with Carl Fontana back with Cosmo, what was his name, Cosmo Walters, the head of the band up there at LSU. He was in that band. And then that was Richard Alexis, and then CJ, the next brother, who was a bass player, went out there, and then Bobby went to LSU. So he wasn't around but just a very short time with the band. Bobby played the string bass?
Bobby was a string bass player.
